title: Section 1: Short title, extent and commencement
text:
Section 1: Short title, extent and commencement:
(1) This Ordinance may be called the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001.
(2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at once.
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

title: Section 7: Powers of Banking Court
text:
Section 7: Powers of Banking Court:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, a Banking Court shall, in all matters with respect to which procedure has not been provided in this Ordinance, exercise all the powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).
(2) A Banking Court shall in all matters with respect to which procedure has not been provided in this Ordinance follow the procedure specified in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

title: Section 9: Procedure of Banking Court
text:
Section 9: Procedure of Banking Court:
(1) Where a customer or a financial institution commits a default in fulfillment of any obligation with regard to any finance, the financial institution or the customer may institute a suit in the Banking Court by presenting a plaint which shall be verified on oath.
(2) The plaint shall be supported by a statement of account and relevant security documents.
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

title: Section 10: Leave to defend
text:
Section 10: Leave to defend:
(1) The defendant shall not be entitled to defend the suit unless he obtains leave from the Banking Court as hereinafter provided.
(2) An application for leave to defend shall be filed within thirty days of the date of first service of summons.
(3) The application for leave to defend shall disclose summary of defenses and specific questions of law or fact.
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

title: Section 15: Sale of mortgaged property without intervention of court
title_only: Sale of mortgaged property without intervention of court
text:
Section 15: Sale of mortgaged property without intervention of court:
(1) In this section, 'mortgage' means a mortgage created by deposit of title deeds, or an English mortgage, or an equitable mortgage.
(2) In case of default by a customer, the financial institution may send a notice to the customer demanding payment.
(3) If the customer fails to pay the amount within thirty days, the financial institution may cause the mortgaged property to be valued by an approved evaluator and sold by public auction.
(4) Judicial Note: Section 15 in its original form was declared unconstitutional and ultra vires by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in National Bank of Pakistan v. Saf Textile Mills Ltd. (PLD 2014 SC 283) for violating Articles 10A, 24, and 25 of the Constitution. Subsequent statutory amendments were enacted under Act XXXVIII of 2016 to introduce structured statutory safeguards, fresh valuation requirements, public notice, and reserve price protections.
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

court_challenges.case_name: National Bank of Pakistan v. Saf Textile Mills Ltd.
court_challenges.ruling: Declared Section 15 of FIO 2001 ultra vires the Constitution as it lacked due process and judicial oversight.
court_challenges.effective_legal_effect: Section 15 struck down; subsequent legislative re-enactment in 2016 introduced mandatory notice, valuation, and reserve price safeguards.

title: Section 19: Execution of decree
text:
Section 19: Execution of decree:
(1) The Banking Court shall on an application made by the decree-holder proceed to execute the decree or order in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908).
(2) The Banking Court, in executing a decree, shall have all the powers of a Civil Court in executing a decree, and shall follow the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including Order XXI thereof, save as otherwise provided in this Ordinance.
(3) The Banking Court may order the sale of mortgaged property, and in executing a decree by sale of mortgaged property, the Banking Court may, on its own motion or on the application of any party, determine the reserve price and the terms and conditions of sale.
(4) Fresh valuation of the mortgaged property shall not be necessary where an authentic valuation has been carried out by an approved evaluator within one year prior to the sale proclamation, unless the Banking Court, for reasons to be recorded in writing, considers a fresh valuation necessary.
(5) The proclamation of sale shall be drawn up and published in accordance with the procedure prescribed by Order XXI Rule 66 and Rule 67 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
(6) Any objection to the execution sale on the ground of material irregularity or fraud shall be governed by Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, subject to the deposit requirement specified in the second proviso thereof (not exceeding twenty per cent of the sum realized at the sale).
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001

title: Section 22: Appeal
text:
Section 22: Appeal:
(1) Any person aggrieved by any final judgment, decree, sentence or final order passed by a Banking Court may, within thirty days of the date of such judgment, decree, sentence or order, prefer an appeal to the High Court.
(2) No appeal shall lie from an interlocutory order which does not dispose of the entire case before the Banking Court.
gazette_reference: Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 30th August, 2001
